definitions.gloss: dizziness upon standing; lightheadedness when standing up
definitions.explanation: A brief spell of dizziness or lightheadedness caused by standing up too quickly. Medically related to a sudden drop in blood pressure (orthostatic hypotension).

examples.japanese: {急|きゅう}に{立|た}ったら{立|た}ちくらみがした。
examples.english: I got dizzy when I stood up suddenly.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}{立|た}ちくらみが{多|おお}いので{病院|びょういん}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: I've been having frequent dizzy spells when standing, so I went to the hospital.

examples.japanese: {貧血|ひんけつ}ぎみで、お{風呂|ふろ}から{上|あ}がるときに{立|た}ちくらみを{起|お}こすことがある。
examples.english: I tend to be anemic, and sometimes I get lightheaded when getting out of the bath.

notes:
A compound of {立|た}つ (to stand) and くらみ (dizziness, from {眩|くら}む). A common everyday health term.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {立|た}ちくらみがする (to feel dizzy upon standing)
- {立|た}ちくらみを{起|お}こす (to get a dizzy spell)
- {立|た}ちくらみが{多|おお}い (to frequently get lightheaded)

USAGE:
Often mentioned in the context of {貧血|ひんけつ} (anemia) or {低血圧|ていけつあつ} (low blood pressure). A very relatable complaint in daily Japanese conversation, especially in hot weather or after bathing.
